table.title: [adversarial] Rowspan taller than its rows
table.html:
StepOwnerNotes
PlanAnaAll three steps share one change ticket. Approval from the security review board is required before any production access is granted, and every action must be logged in the audit trail with the ticket number, the operator's name and the exact commands executed.
BuildBen
ShipCai

understanding.purpose: Show the owner of each workflow step alongside a note shared by all three steps.
understanding.reading: Readers scan the steps and owners row by row, then read the merged note as context for the whole sequence. The shared note can make the three-row group taller than the step and owner labels require.
groups: Step and Owner form compact row-by-row pairs; Notes applies to all three pairs as a group.
keep_intact: Unbreakable words in the shared note
may_wrap: The shared note at word boundaries; its merged cell can use the height of all three rows.

preferred.name: r3B
preferred.note: Give the shared note a modest increase in width to explore a different four-line wrap, while retaining comfortable space for the paired row labels.

acceptable.name: r1A
acceptable.note: Give Step and Owner modest breathing room beyond their minimum widths while preserving a broad Notes column and the compact four-line group.

acceptable.name: r1B
acceptable.note: Explore a slightly shorter note measure with a more generous Owner column, while keeping the row-by-row labels compact enough to avoid the excessive whitespace of r0C.

acceptable.name: r1C
acceptable.note: Test a narrower overall table with a shorter Notes measure and compact label columns; compare the benefit of shorter lines against any added wrapping or row height.

acceptable.name: r2A
acceptable.note: Keep the compact label columns and give Notes a middle width. This tests whether a little more space than r1C improves the note's line endings while retaining a right margin.

acceptable.name: r2B
acceptable.note: Reduce Step and Owner while keeping their headers intact, and give the recovered space to Notes. This tests whether the widest feasible note produces a better four-line rhythm.

acceptable.name: r3A
acceptable.note: Keep r2A’s comfortable Step and Notes widths while reclaiming 5px from Owner; its 59px text area still accommodates the 48px header.

bad.name: r0C
bad.note: Give the paired step and owner columns equal visual weight, accepting more lines in the shared note.
bad.why: The short Step and Owner columns take almost half the width, leaving the shared note cramped. Its six lines stretch all three data rows and leave conspicuous empty space in the first two columns.

rationale: r3B gives the short step and owner labels enough room while reserving most of the width for the note shared across all three rows. The note fits in four lines, and the three data rows remain even and easy to scan. A small margin inside the viewport gives the table a comfortable right edge.

general: Allocate width according to content and its role, rather than making columns equal by default.
A cell spanning several rows can determine the height of all of them, so its wrapping affects the rhythm of the whole table.
specific: The Step and Owner values are short, while the shared note is much longer and benefits from most of the available width.
Several note widths produce the same four-line wrap, leaving room to choose based on line endings and the table's overall proportion.

tradeoffs: A full-width design such as r1A gives the note more horizontal room; the slightly narrower r3B leaves a visible viewport margin while retaining four lines.
uncertain: The ranges are approximate visual judgments, not tested wrap thresholds. Reasonable designers may prefer another four-line candidate for its line endings or its use of the full viewport.

critique.good: The compact Step and Owner columns keep each pair easy to scan, while the broad Notes column holds the shared text in four lines. All labels and words stay intact.
critique.problems: The first two columns feel tight against their content, particularly the Step header and Build label; the long note lines also dominate the table.
critique.cause: Step and Owner are at their minimum content widths of 56px and 69px, leaving 594px for Notes.

critique.good: The step and owner pairs have comfortable breathing room, and the shared note remains four lines tall. The table has a clear hierarchy and fits the viewport.
critique.problems: The two short-label columns occupy more space than their contents need, while the note still forms relatively long lines.
critique.cause: Widths of 90px and 110px allocate 200px to the compact labels, leaving 519px for Notes.

critique.good: The wider label columns make the step and owner pairs distinct, and the shorter note lines are easy to follow.
critique.problems: Large empty areas in the first two columns weaken the connection between each step and its owner. The six-line note also stretches the three rows, producing a loose vertical rhythm.
critique.cause: Giving both label columns 175px leaves only 369px for Notes, increasing wrapping and forcing the merged cell and its rows taller.

critique.good: The compact Step and Owner columns keep each pair easy to scan, while the shared note has a clear, continuous reading area. All labels and words remain intact.
critique.problems: The note extends into a fourth line, leaving the three rows taller than their short labels need. Its last line is noticeably short.
critique.cause: The 562px Notes column gives the text enough width for four lines but not enough to fit it into three within the available table width.

critique.good: The wider Step and Owner columns give the row labels more breathing room, and the note remains intact and readable.
critique.problems: The first two columns have substantially more space than their content needs. The narrower note still takes four lines, with more frequent line breaks.
critique.cause: The 90px and 125px widths reserve 58px more for Step and Owner than r1A, reducing Notes to 504px.

critique.good: The compact label columns preserve a clear row-by-row pairing, and the narrower overall table leaves useful space at the viewport edge. The note still fits in four lines.
critique.problems: The note is more densely wrapped, and the unused space to the right could support a more relaxed line length.
critique.cause: The 480px Notes column leaves 82px of available table width unused compared with r1A.

critique.good: The step and owner labels are easy to scan as row pairs. The shared note fits in four lines without splitting words, and the table sits comfortably inside the viewport.
critique.problems: The Owner column has a little more space than its short labels need. The note’s last line is shorter than the lines above it, though the ragged edge remains reasonably balanced.
critique.cause: The 85px Owner width leaves 64px for text, more than the 48px needed for its header. The 520px Notes width determines the four-line wrap.

critique.good: All labels remain intact, and the wider note is easy to read across the three-row group. The table uses the available viewport width.
critique.problems: The note ends with a particularly short fourth line, leaving a conspicuous blank area in the merged cell. The compact first two columns also feel less generous than in r2A.
critique.cause: The 582px Notes width changes the line breaks without reducing the note below four lines. The 62px Step width leaves only 41px for text.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

ref_equal.why: The short Step and Owner entries occupy two thirds of the table, leaving Notes cramped and creating excessive row height and empty space.

ref_auto.why: Compact Step and Owner columns keep their labels intact and give the shared note ample room; the three rows remain easy to scan.

r1A.why: The first two columns have comfortable breathing room while the shared note remains readable in four lines, with clear row boundaries.

r3B.why: The columns are well balanced and the note reads comfortably, though the unused space at the right could give the table slightly more room.

r1B.why: The rows and shared note are clear, but the short Step and Owner entries have more space than they need.

r0C.why: All text stays intact, but the wide Step and Owner columns leave the note narrower, making it wrap more and stretching the rows.

raw.unsure: B is more economical with space; C gives the first two columns a little more breathing room. Both read well.

r3B.why: The compact Step and Owner columns give the shared note room to read in four lines, with clear rows and a small right margin.

r0C.why: Step and Owner take much more space than their short entries need, leaving the shared note cramped into six lines and making the rows unusually tall.

r1B.why: The note reads comfortably in four lines, though Step and Owner have more spare width than their contents need.

r1A.why: Compact identifier columns leave generous space for the four-line note, while the three steps remain easy to scan.

ref_auto.why: The narrow Step and Owner columns still fit their contents, giving the shared note the most room and keeping its four lines easy to read.

ref_equal.why: The oversized Step and Owner columns squeeze the note into a narrow, ten-line strip, producing very tall rows and excessive empty space.

raw.unsure: A, D and E are close: all keep the note to four lines and the short entries intact, with small differences in column spacing and line breaks.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
